task: night research round 2 - scan_hypotheses (focus: precision of x138 safe-division forks: I-081 DaughterNet veto, I-072 float-coord gates, density-quartile reading of exp60 gates)
summary: Label-free measurements on the exp60 dumps (676 safe forks, 56 clips) and on the 151 GT train divisions give one clear new arm. ANTIPAR vetoes a safe-division fork when its daughters leave on the same side of the parent: cos(c1-P, c2-P) > 0.25, the cos_max already frozen in the insertion rule. It flags 16.7% of x138 safe forks but only 4.6% of real GT divisions. That implies a vetoed-fork precision of ~0.08-0.15, well under the 0.265 break-even. I-081 (DaughterNet veto) cannot be read from divins_dump: only 5% of forks have p for all three nodes. It becomes testable after an OOF CPU re-score with the local fold weights, and the threshold is already GT-calibrated: p_par(P) < 0.057 = GT parent 5th percentile, OOF. I-072 is closed. x138 gates already run on float coordinates, and re-gating on final coordinates targets geometry that 38-47% of real divisions have. Young-parent, refractory, stub-branch and div3 flags are closed on GT evidence. Density quartiles: GT divisions are flat (25/24/23/27) while safe forks grow 55 to 263, so the FP-fork mass sits in the dense quartiles; add a frozen density column and a dense-half no-harm clause. Urgent: freeze these rules in CONTEXT before anyone cross-reads per-fork labels. The forkblob harm gate already FAILED at 20:04 UTC and the T9 score is presumably next. No fork labels were looked at in this scan.

findings.what: ANTIPAR fork veto (R3 class; nodes untouched). Rule: for every 2-child fork with exactly one safe_division edge and no div_inserted edge, on FINAL coordinates, compute cos = (c_safe-P).(c_ilp-P) / (|.||.| + 1e-9). If cos > 0.25, drop one edge with forkmid's convention: the ILP-side edge if its edge_prob == 0.0, else the added edge. Runs after forkmid and before forkblob, fail-soft, ANTIPAR_ENABLE default 0, byte-identical when off. Mechanism: at mitosis the daughters separate on opposite sides of the parent (GT median cos -0.75). A same-side pair is a duplicate or neighbour detection that the ranker (parent_dist + 0.15*sister) prefers. Expected gain: public safe forks ~29 clips x 12 = ~350, of which 17% are flagged = ~58, and ~4-5% are evaluable = ~2-3. Each FP removed is worth ~+0.001 (J 0.33 on ~22 public GT divisions: 11/32 vs 11/33) and each TP removed ~-0.003. At q ~0.1 the gain is ~+0.0015; center, halved for GT-to-prediction transfer and evaluable-share doubt, ~+0.0007 public (range -0.002..+0.003), private similar. P(<0) ~0.25. Runtime < 1 s per clip, i.e. ~0 of the ~4 h headroom.
findings.evidence: Label-free dose, 56 clips: 113/676 safe forks flagged (16.7%; SELECTION 59/345, CONFIRMATION 54/331; 44b6 32/235, 6bba 81/441). GT, 151 train divisions: 7 flagged (4.6%) [cos>0: 10.6% vs 21.3%; cos>0.5: 3.3% vs 5.8%]. The part outside forkblob/forkmid (cos>0.25 AND sister>5 AND mid<4.5) holds 25 predicted forks and 0 GT divisions. On shard A, 14 of 16 forkmid forks are also flagged. Bayes: p = 0.25 evaluable precision and a GT-like TP flag rate of 4.6% give q = 0.0115/0.152 = 0.076; with the TP flag rate doubled by position noise, q ~0.15 (< 0.265). Scripts: session scratchpad dose.py, dose_all.py, gtstats.py; numbers in scan_hypotheses.notes.md.

findings.what: DNVETO, which is I-081 made testable: a DaughterNet parent veto on safe-division forks with a GT-calibrated threshold. Veto (same edge convention) when p_par(P) < 0.057, the 5th percentile of OOF p_par on the 151 GT parents, so by construction <= 5% of real divisions fall below it. Kernel: the divinsert cell already loads the 5 fold models. Score the fork parents (~12 per clip) with the 5-fold mean, adding < 2 s per clip, i.e. ~0 of the headroom. Lab: score each clip's fork parents with ONLY its OOF fold model (splits.json fold; tools/daughternet.score_nodes(model_index=fold)) from the local train zarr. Expected dose ~20-25%: position-matched OOF p_par of 184 fork parents has 25th percentile 0.068 and 5th 0.011. The enrichment is ~4x, weaker evidence than ANTIPAR because the matching is approximate and the 5-model mean is calibrated differently from a single fold. Prior: the DivNet parent veto p<0.5 (I-058) scored lab +0.0023 with 59 FP / 1 TP removed, then tied on LB (probe 20). Expected +0.0005 public center, P(<0) ~0.3.

findings.what: Close I-072 (divergence/symmetry gates on float coordinates). Its premise is false: x138's add_safe_divisions_postlink already runs on the presafe graph, whose coordinates are float and head-refined. The only new variant is re-gating on FINAL (linefit-smoothed) coordinates with x138's own thresholds. It would veto 30% of forks (sym > 0.6: 53, div2 < 2.25: 63 of 329). But real GT divisions have exactly that geometry: sym > 0.6 in 38% and 1-step divergence < 2.25 um in 47%, against 16% and 19% of predicted forks. Not enriched, so it is TP-hostile. Also closed on the same GT evidence: young-parent veto (GT 21% vs pred 9%), refractory/cell-cycle veto (GT 0, pred 1%: no dose), 3-step divergence < 3 um (GT 34%), and stub-daughter-branch veto (GT 44% because sparse annotation truncates tracks, so it cannot be calibrated).

findings.what: Density-quartile reading (I-204) for the exp60 fork arms. Quartiles are frozen on nodes/frame of the control final graph (label-free; edges 83.7 / 160.7 / 258.8, 14 clips each). GT divisions are flat across them (25/24/23/27) while x138 safe forks rise 55/149/209/263: 2.2 forks per GT division in Q0 vs 9.7 in Q3. The FP-fork mass, and so both the gain and the harm of every fork veto, sits in Q1-Q3. The ANTIPAR flag follows the same pattern (5/31/37/40), as do sister<=5 (14/37/44/65) and mid>=4.5 (1/12/10/17). A pooled lab gate is dominated by dense clips anyway. The guard needed is that no TP is lost in the densest quartile, where private embryos may be denser than public.

findings.what: forkmid (C04/K3) carries more geometric TP risk than its exp39 prior suggests: 17% of real GT divisions (25/151) have |P - mid(c1,c2)| >= 4.5 um, against 5.9% of x138 safe forks (40/676). The mid rule is therefore NOT enriched for FPs; its lab 11 FP / 0 TP came from exp39 graphs, where 4.5 um was also chosen. ANTIPAR contains almost all forkmid forks (14/16 on shard A) at a GT flag rate of 4.6%, so it is the geometric criterion with less TP risk. Sister <= 5 um is strongly enriched (GT 3.3% vs pred 23.7%; GT sister 5th pct 5.4 um vs pred median 6.8), but forkblob, the only frozen rule using it, failed its harm gate at 20:04 UTC. findings.what: Structural facts about x138 safe divisions that matter for any veto design. The per-video and per-frame caps NEVER bind (safe_division_skipped_cap = 0 on all 28 shard-A clips), so an in-stage veto frees no slot, and post-hoc vetoes (R3 class, nodes untouched) behave exactly like in-stage ones for the fork set. DaughterNet p in divins_dump covers only insertion-triple nodes, so fork parents are missing. The ILP-side edge of 25% of safe forks has edge_prob == 0.0, so forkmid's edge-drop convention decides the kept edge for a quarter of vetoes and must be the same for all vetoes. All lab clips have T = 100 frames.
